stem: In children, what is the most frequent location of intussusception?

options.text: Location will always depend on the location of a lead point lesion

explanation: The commonest intussusception in infants and young children is ileocolic, where the terminal ileum telescopes into the colon. This fits the typical age group and presentation of episodic pain, vomiting, and red currant jelly stool.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Abdominal pain

optionExplanations.A: Not the usual most frequent paediatric pattern.
optionExplanations.B: This is not the commonest location in children.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Ileocolic intussusception is the most frequent type in children.
optionExplanations.D: Lead points can contribute, but the commonest location is still ileocolic.
optionExplanations.E: Gastric intussusception is rare and not the typical paediatric form.

Clinical Scenario 2 - Timmy

Next, you are taking a more detailed history about eight month old Timmy. He has a one day history of screaming inconsolably and poor feeding. He has also vomited breast milk twice over the past few hours. His mother has not measured any fever; there is no diarrhoea and no cold symptoms. When Timmy’s mother last changed the nappy, she noted some 'red currant jelly-like' substance. She has noted that between bouts of screaming, Timmy has been calm and at times quite sleepy.

The following five questions refer to Timmy’s clinical scenario.
